Latin word

omnia

omnia, omnium n. pl.

adjective used as a noun (neuter plural of omnis), declension

everything, all things

In this lexicon

  • everything

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 16.4.4: omnia dēpōne; Cic. Sen. 21: omnia quae cūrant meminērunt

  • omnia complectēns: comprehensive

    classical

  • Nē committās omnia ūnī nāvī.: don’t put all your eggs in one basket

    modern

  • ante omnia: firstly

    classical

  • omnia jūra: full access

    * our formation

  • labor omnia vīcit improbus: hard work conquers all

    classical

  • Labor vincit omnia.: hard work conquers all

    modern

  • ante omnia: priority

    classical

  • omnia dīvēndita sunt: sold out

    modern

  • Tempus omnia revēlat.: time brings everything to light

    modern

  • Tempus omnia sānat.: time heals all wounds

    modern

  • omnia miscēre: topsy-turvy

    classical

    we expect to reach Tusculum on the Nones or the day after. Have everything ready thereCic. Fam. 14.20.1
